PNC reported that its tangible book value increased due to improvements in Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (AOCI), specifically noting a $2.6 billion improvement in AOCI in the fourth quarter of 2023 driven by lower interest rates, which raised tangible book value per share to $85.08. PNC also highlighted that as lower-rate securities and swaps roll off, they expect continued meaningful improvement to tangible book value from AOCI accretion.

Fifth Third reported that its tangible book value per share grew nearly 30% during the fourth quarter of 2023 due to strong earnings and a rally in interest rates. To manage future capital volatility related to AOCI, Fifth Third moved $12.6 billion of securities from available-for-sale (AFS) to held-to-maturity (HTM), an action expected to de-risk potential AOCI volatility to capital by about 30% if market rates rise again.
